hook.line: On your first day, or when you explain a job to a friend, someone asks what it actually involves. Spanish has one tidy verb for that.

examples.es: Mi trabajo consiste en preparar el café.
examples.en: My job involves making the coffee.

examples.es: La prueba consiste en traducir un texto.
examples.en: The test consists of translating a text.

examples.es: La oferta de Altamira consiste en comprar toda la cuadra.
examples.en: Altamira's offer consists of buying the whole block.

examples.es: Las pruebas consisten en traducir textos.
examples.en: The tests consist of translating texts.

examples.es: El proyecto no consiste en vender el café.
examples.en: The project isn't about selling the café.

rule:
*Consistir en* says what something is made up of or involves. The word after *en* is a noun or an infinitive: *consiste en atender*, *consiste en un texto*.

The preposition is always *en*. English "consist of" tempts you to say *de*; don't.

The verb agrees with the thing: *consiste*, *consisten*.

To ask, use *¿En qué consiste…?*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a fixed preposition (a prepositional complement).

readAndPick.es: La receta consiste en mezclar la harina y los huevos.
options: The recipe involves mixing the flour and eggs.
The recipe is kept in the flour and eggs.
The recipe is mixed with flour and eggs.
Where is your job? (to a friend)
What does your job involve? (to a friend)
Who is your job? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Las pruebas consisten en traducir textos.
options: The test consists of translating a text.
The tests consist of translating a text.
The tests consist of translating texts.

readAndPick.es: El problema consiste en que no hay plata.
options: The problem is that there is no money.
The problem is in the bank.
The problem will cost money.

readAndPick.es: La prueba consiste en traducir un texto.
options: The test consists of translating a text.
The tests consist of translating a text.
The test is a translated text.

readAndPick.es: El proyecto no consiste en vender el café.
options: The project is about selling the café.
The project isn't about selling the café.
The café isn't part of the project.

readAndPick.es: La oferta de Altamira consiste en comprar toda la cuadra.
options: Altamira's offer consists of selling the whole block.
Altamira's offer consists of buying the whole block.
Altamira's offer is on the whole block.
What does the meeting involve?
When is the meeting?
Where is the meeting?

readAndPick.es: Mi trabajo consiste en atender a los clientes.
options: My job involves serving customers.
My job is with the customers.
My job has no customers.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *en* or *de* and type the whole sentence: *El trabajo consiste ___ atender a los clientes.*
yourTurn.answer: El trabajo consiste en atender a los clientes.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What does the process involve?
yourTurn.why: *¿En qué consiste…?* is the way to ask what something involves.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: My job involves making the coffee.
yourTurn.answer: Mi trabajo consiste en preparar el café.
yourTurn.why: *Consiste en* plus an infinitive says what the job involves.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: What does your job involve?
yourTurn.why: *Tu trabajo* is one thing, so the verb stays *consiste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *La prueba consiste en traducir un texto.* Say: The tests consist of translating texts.
yourTurn.answer: Las pruebas consisten en traducir textos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, using *consistir en*: The project isn't about selling the café.
yourTurn.answer: El proyecto no consiste en vender el café.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Altamira's offer consists of buying the whole block.
yourTurn.answer: La oferta de Altamira consiste en comprar toda la cuadra.

pitfalls.wrong: El trabajo consiste de atender a los clientes.
pitfalls.right: El trabajo consiste en atender a los clientes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "consist of", but Spanish uses *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Las pruebas consiste en traducir textos.
pitfalls.right: Las pruebas consisten en traducir textos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Two tests need the plural verb *consisten*.

pitfalls.wrong: El trabajo consiste en atendiendo a los clientes.
pitfalls.right: El trabajo consiste en atender a los clientes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *en* Spanish uses the infinitive, not *-ando*.

personal: Explain your own job or a hobby in one sentence, starting with *Mi trabajo consiste en…* or *Lo que hago consiste en…*.
